verdict.headline: This NDA is balanced, mutual, and aligns with standard market terms.
summary: The agreement applies standard mutual obligations with customary carve-outs and practical exceptions.
Durations, remedies, assignment rules, and dispute resolution mechanisms follow fair commercial standards.
No high-risk clauses or unbalanced terms were identified.

verdict.headline: Highly one-sided NDA imposing perpetual liability, no standard carve-outs, and zero protection for the bakery's own secrets.
summary: The agreement is entirely one-sided, leaving the bakery's recipes, pricing, and tender submissions completely unprotected while exposing it to perpetual liability.
It eliminates all standard carve-outs and forbids disclosure even when required by law or to professional advisers.
The bakery is barred from terminating the contract and must give a broad indemnity with no mutual rights.

findings.title: Confidential information includes public data and pre-existing knowledge
findings.quote: "Confidential Information" means all information of any kind whatsoever, in any form or medium, whether or not marked as confidential, that is disclosed to or obtained by the Recipient or its Representatives in connection with the Purpose or the Proposed Arrangement, including recipes, product specifications, supplier lists, pricing, volumes, sales data, outlet information, business plans, and any information that the Recipient already holds or that is in the public domain, together with all notes, analyses and other materials prepared by the Recipient that contain or reflect any such information.
findings.why_risky: Defining confidential information to include items already known or in the public domain makes normal business operations impossible without risking breach.
findings.standard: Confidential information should only cover non-public information disclosed for the project, with standard carve-outs for public knowledge or prior possession.
findings.suggested_ask: Please narrow the definition of Confidential Information to non-public information disclosed for the discussions, and remove public and pre-existing information.

findings.title: Complete exclusion of carve-outs and compelled disclosure exception
findings.quote: The Recipient's obligations under this Agreement apply without exception, irrespective of whether any Confidential Information is or becomes publicly available, was already known to the Recipient, or is required to be disclosed by any law, regulation or order of any court or authority.
findings.why_risky: Removing the legal requirement exception forces you to breach either the contract or a court order/law if subpoenaed or audited.
findings.standard: Standard NDAs must include the four typical carve-outs and explicitly allow legally compelled disclosures.
findings.suggested_ask: Please add the standard four exceptions and permit disclosures required by law, regulation, or court order.

findings.title: Completely one-sided confidentiality with open sharing of recipient data
findings.quote: The Discloser gives no undertaking of confidentiality in respect of any information provided to it by the Recipient, including the Recipient's tender, pricing and product samples, and may use and share such information with its Affiliates and other suppliers as it sees fit.
findings.why_risky: The vendor can legally share your proprietary recipes, product pricing, and tender submissions directly with your competitor suppliers.
findings.standard: NDAs should be mutual when both parties share confidential commercial or technical information.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the confidentiality obligations mutual so that our proprietary pricing, product samples, and tender data are equally protected.

findings.title: Perpetual confidentiality obligations
findings.quote: The Recipient's obligations under this Agreement shall continue in perpetuity and shall survive the completion or abandonment of the Proposed Arrangement and any termination of this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: Perpetual secrecy for ordinary commercial and operational discussions creates indefinite liability risk.
findings.standard: A balanced confidentiality period lasts 2 to 3 years after disclosure, with perpetual protection reserved solely for genuine trade secrets.
findings.suggested_ask: Please limit the confidentiality duration to two years after disclosure, reserving longer protection only for genuine trade secrets.

findings.title: One-sided termination right
findings.quote: Only the Discloser may terminate this Agreement, by written notice to the Recipient at any time.
findings.why_risky: You cannot formally terminate the agreement if discussions collapse, leaving you locked into an active contract controlled solely by the vendor.
findings.standard: Either party should be able to end an NDA upon written notice at any time.
findings.suggested_ask: Please allow either party to terminate this agreement upon written notice.

findings.title: Prohibition on sharing with professional advisers
findings.quote: not disclose the Confidential Information to any person other than its Representatives, and not to its professional advisers, contractors or financiers, without the prior written consent of the Discloser;
findings.why_risky: You cannot consult your own lawyers, accountants, or financiers regarding the tender without prior written approval from the other party.
findings.standard: Recipients should be allowed to share information on a need-to-know basis with professional advisers bound by confidentiality duties.
findings.suggested_ask: Please permit disclosure on a need-to-know basis to our professional legal, financial, and accounting advisers.

findings.title: Mandatory destruction of backups and statutory declaration requirement
findings.quote: Within five (5) days of a written request from the Discloser, the Recipient shall return to the Discloser, or at the Discloser's option destroy, all documents and materials containing Confidential Information, including all copies held electronically and in back-up systems, and shall deliver to the Discloser a statutory declaration made by a director of the Recipient confirming that it has done so.
findings.why_risky: Purging all automated electronic backups within five days is technically impractical and demands an onerous formal statutory declaration.
findings.standard: Agreements should allow routine electronic backups and legal-compliance archives to be retained under continued confidentiality.
findings.suggested_ask: Please allow copies stored on routine electronic backup systems to be retained under continuing confidentiality, and remove the statutory declaration requirement.

findings.title: Broad one-sided indemnity for any breach
findings.quote: The Recipient shall indemnify the Discloser and its Affiliates against all losses, costs (including legal costs on a full indemnity basis) and expenses arising from any breach of this Agreement by the Recipient or its Representatives.
findings.why_risky: Full indemnity shifting, including legal fees on a full indemnity basis for any alleged breach, shifts excessive financial risk onto you.
findings.standard: NDAs typically rely on ordinary contract damages and injunctive relief rather than one-sided indemnity clauses.
findings.suggested_ask: Please remove the indemnity clause and rely on ordinary contract damages and injunctions.

findings.title: One-sided assignment right
findings.quote: The Discloser may assign this Agreement or any of its rights under it to any of its Affiliates or to any purchaser of its business. The Recipient may not assign this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: The vendor can transfer the agreement freely to affiliates or buyers, while you are blocked from transferring it even in a corporate sale.
findings.standard: Assignment restrictions should be mutual, permitting transfer to a business successor upon a merger or acquisition.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the assignment rule mutual: no assignment without consent, except to a successor in a merger or sale of the business.

missing_clauses.title: Dispute Escalation and Talks
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The contract defaults directly to court litigation in Singapore with no preliminary negotiation or mediation steps, which is extremely expensive for a Malaysian SME.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please provide for good-faith talks and mediation before any formal court proceedings.

verdict.headline: High-risk agreement containing severe non-compete restrictions, heavy liquidated damages, and distant foreign jurisdiction.
summary: This NDA imposes an aggressive 3-year non-compete across ASEAN that could shut down your existing core business.
It demands uncapped liquidated damages of USD 250,000 per breach plus legal fees under New York law and courts.
The confidentiality obligations are strictly one-way and assignment rights are heavily unbalanced.

findings.title: Severe non-compete blocking existing operations
findings.quote: 6.2 Accordingly, during the term of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years thereafter, the Counterparty shall not, and shall procure that its affiliates, directors and shareholders shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, develop, market or invest in any business that competes with any business of the Group anywhere in the Territory, including the design or sale of irrigation controllers, soil sensors or farm analytics software.
findings.why_risky: This clause prohibits your company, directors, and shareholders from operating in your existing core market across Southeast Asia for up to 6 years, potentially forcing you to cease current business operations.
findings.standard: A standard NDA protects disclosed information and must never contain a non-compete clause.
findings.suggested_ask: Please delete Section 6 entirely; an NDA should only protect confidential information without restricting our ability to carry out our legitimate business.

findings.title: Uncapped liquidated damages per breach
findings.quote: 8.2 In addition to any other remedy, the Counterparty shall pay to Halvexa, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, the sum of USD 250,000 for each breach of this Agreement, without any limit on the aggregate amount payable, together with all attorneys' fees and costs incurred by Halvexa in enforcing this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: USD 250,000 per violation with no cap and a clause defining every day of breach as a separate occurrence could quickly bankrupt a small company for minor or accidental issues.
findings.standard: Market-standard NDAs do not include fixed liquidated damages sums; injured parties rely on ordinary actual damages and injunctive relief.
findings.suggested_ask: Please remove the liquidated damages clause and rely on ordinary damages and injunctions.

findings.title: Exclusive New York governing law and jurisdiction
findings.quote: 10.2 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, and waives any objection to venue in such courts, including any objection that such courts are an inconvenient forum.
findings.why_risky: Litigating in New York courts is prohibitively expensive for a Malaysian SME and makes defending any claim or minor allegation financially unfeasible.
findings.standard: For transactions concerning distribution in Malaysia, governing law and dispute forums should be local (Malaysia or Singapore).
findings.suggested_ask: Please change the governing law to Malaysian law with the courts of Kuala Lumpur, or Singapore law with SIAC arbitration.

findings.title: One-way confidentiality obligations
findings.quote: 2.1 The Counterparty shall hold the Confidential Information in confidence, use it solely for the purpose of evaluating the Transaction, and disclose it only to its Representatives on a need-to-know basis, provided that such Representatives are informed of its confidential nature.
findings.why_risky: Only Lumio Tani Agritech is bound to keep information confidential. Any information your company shares with Halvexa receives no protection under this agreement.
findings.standard: NDAs exploring commercial deals where both parties share information should be mutual.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the confidentiality undertakings mutual so both parties protect each other's proprietary information.

findings.title: Restriction on accepting customer or distributor business
findings.quote: 6.3 During the same period, the Counterparty shall not solicit, or accept business from, any person that was a customer or distributor of the Group in the Territory at any time during the term of this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: You are forbidden from doing business with anyone who dealt with Halvexa across ASEAN, even if they approach you independently without any solicitation.
findings.standard: Non-solicit covenants should be narrow, mutual, and should not prevent a business from accepting unsolicited work or ordinary commercial dealings.
findings.suggested_ask: Please delete Section 6.3 or remove the restriction on accepting unsolicited business.

findings.title: One-sided assignment right
findings.quote: 9.1 Halvexa may assign this Agreement to any member of the Group without the Counterparty's consent. The Counterparty shall not assign this Agreement without Halvexa's prior written consent.
findings.why_risky: Halvexa can transfer this agreement and its rights to any affiliated entity without asking, while Lumio Tani Agritech cannot assign even in a reorganization or sale of the business.
findings.standard: Assignment rules should be mutual, requiring written consent unless transferring to a business successor in a merger or sale.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the assignment rule mutual: no assignment without consent, except to a successor in a merger or sale of the business.

missing_clauses.title: Mutual confidentiality protection
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The agreement defines Confidential Information only as disclosures made by Halvexa, leaving your company's proprietary data and commercial information unprotected.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please expand the definition of confidential information and Section 2 to protect both parties equally.

missing_clauses.title: Mutual IP ownership and reservation of rights
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The agreement confirms Halvexa's ownership of IP but does not explicitly protect your ownership of pre-existing intellectual property and independent developments.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a clause confirming that each party retains full ownership of its own pre-existing intellectual property and independently developed products.

verdict.headline: One-sided NDA leaving your operational data unprotected, with one-way termination and long restrictions.
summary: The agreement expressly denies any confidentiality protection for your fleet operational data while binding you strictly.
Only the vendor may terminate early, and you are bound by an unusually long 5-year confidentiality period plus a 24-month non-solicitation restriction.
The contract should be made mutual in obligations, assignment, and termination rights.

findings.title: One-sided confidentiality leaving receiver data unprotected
findings.quote: Obligasi kerahsiaan di bawah Perjanjian ini dikenakan ke atas Penerima sahaja. Pihak Pendedah tidak mempunyai sebarang obligasi kerahsiaan terhadap maklumat yang diberikan oleh Penerima kepadanya, termasuk data operasi armada Penerima yang dikongsi semasa projek rintis.
findings.why_risky: The vendor explicitly disclaims any duty to protect information you share with them, including sensitive fleet operations data shared during the pilot project.
findings.standard: In pilot projects and mutual discussions where both parties exchange information, confidentiality obligations should be bilateral.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the confidentiality obligations mutual so that our fleet and operational data shared during the pilot are equally protected.

findings.title: One-sided early termination right
findings.quote: Pihak Pendedah boleh menamatkan Perjanjian ini pada bila-bila masa dengan memberikan notis bertulis kepada Penerima. Penerima tidak boleh menamatkan Perjanjian ini sebelum tamat tempoh tersebut tanpa persetujuan bertulis Pihak Pendedah.
findings.why_risky: Only the discloser can terminate the agreement at will, locking you in for the full five-year term unless they agree to release you.
findings.standard: Either party should be entitled to terminate the NDA upon written notice at any time.
findings.suggested_ask: Please allow either party to terminate the agreement at any time by giving written notice.

findings.title: Excessively long agreement and confidentiality term
findings.quote: Perjanjian ini berkuat kuasa pada Tarikh Berkuat Kuasa dan akan kekal berkuat kuasa bagi suatu tempoh lima (5) tahun, dan obligasi Penerima di bawah Fasal 2 akan terus terpakai selama lima (5) tahun selepas tamat atau penamatan Perjanjian ini.
findings.why_risky: A 5-year active term combined with a 5-year survival period creates an effective 10-year lock-in for ordinary business discussions.
findings.standard: Market standard for an NDA is a 1 to 2-year term with confidentiality surviving for 2 to 3 years post-termination.
findings.suggested_ask: Please reduce the agreement term to 1 or 2 years, with confidentiality obligations surviving for 2 years after termination.

findings.title: Excessive and one-sided employee non-solicitation
findings.quote: Penerima tidak boleh, dalam tempoh Perjanjian ini dan bagi tempoh dua puluh empat (24) bulan selepas itu, secara langsung atau tidak langsung memujuk atau menggaji mana-mana pekerja Pihak Pendedah.
findings.why_risky: It binds only you for a lengthy 24-month period post-termination across all vendor staff, with no carve-out for general hiring advertisements.
findings.standard: Non-solicitation clauses in NDAs should be mutual, capped at 6 to 12 months, limited to staff directly encountered during discussions, and exclude general job adverts.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the non-solicitation mutual, reduce the duration to 12 months, limit it to personnel involved in our discussions, and exclude general job advertisements.

findings.title: One-sided assignment restriction
findings.quote: Penerima tidak boleh menyerahhakkan atau memindahkan hak atau obligasinya di bawah Perjanjian ini tanpa persetujuan bertulis Pihak Pendedah terlebih dahulu.
findings.why_risky: Only you are restricted from assigning rights or obligations, leaving the vendor free to assign the contract without your knowledge or consent.
findings.standard: Assignment restrictions should apply equally to both parties, with standard exceptions for business sales or reorganisations.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the assignment restriction mutual so neither party can assign without written consent, except in connection with a merger or sale of the business.

verdict.headline: A well-balanced, market-standard software and services contract with fair terms for both sides.
summary: The terms closely adhere to standard market practices, offering mutual liability protections, clear IP ownership, and data privacy safeguards.

msa-01-fair.disclaimer: This is an automated review to help you prepare. It is not legal advice.

verdict.headline: Dangerous 2-year auto-renewal with strict postal notice, 20% annual price rises, and full payout on early exit.
summary: Missing a 90-day registered post deadline locks you into an extra 24 months with no way out without paying the full remaining term fees.
The vendor can automatically increase fees by 20% each year without advance notice, and you cannot terminate to avoid the hike.
Most other terms including liability caps, confidentiality, IP, and data protection are relatively balanced.

findings.title: Extended 24-month renewal with long 90-day notice window
findings.quote: Upon the expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of twenty-four (24) months each (each a "Renewal Term") unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal to the other party at least ninety (90) days before the expiry of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term.
findings.why_risky: A 90-day notice window is very easy to miss, and missing it locks your company in for a 24-month renewal period, which is double the initial 12-month term.
findings.standard: Renewal terms should match or be shorter than the initial term (typically 12 months) with a 30-day notice window and a vendor reminder.
findings.suggested_ask: Please change renewal to 12-month periods with 30 days' notice to stop renewal, and have the vendor send a written reminder 60 days before the renewal date.

findings.title: Automatic 20% annual price increase with no exit right
findings.quote: With effect from each anniversary of the Effective Date, the Provider shall be entitled to increase the Subscription Fees by twenty per cent (20%) of the Subscription Fees then in effect, without further notice to the Customer. Such increase shall apply automatically and shall not give the Customer any right to terminate this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: A compounding 20% yearly price increase is well above inflation, requires no prior notice, and explicitly bars you from terminating to escape the price hike.
findings.standard: Annual price rises should require at least 60 days' written notice, be capped at 3-5% or inflation, and grant the customer an exit right if rejected.
findings.suggested_ask: Please cap any annual price increase at 5% with 60 days' written notice and allow us to terminate without penalty if we do not accept the increase.

findings.title: Full remaining fees payable upon termination for convenience
findings.quote: The Customer may terminate this Agreement before the end of the Subscription Term for convenience by giving thirty (30) days' written notice, provided that it pays to the Provider, as an early termination charge, all Subscription Fees that would have been payable for the remainder of the then-current Subscription Term.
findings.why_risky: Requiring 100% of the remaining fees makes termination for convenience completely ineffective as a business exit route, especially when locked into a 24-month renewal term.
findings.standard: Termination for convenience should only require payment for services actually rendered and unrecoverable direct committed costs incurred up to the exit date.
findings.suggested_ask: Please remove the charge for all remaining term fees upon convenience termination, requiring only payment for services delivered up to the termination date.

findings.title: Notice of non-renewal restricted to registered post
findings.quote: Notice of non-renewal is effective only if sent by registered post to the Provider's registered office marked for the attention of the Contracts Department. Notice by email or through the Portal shall not be effective for the purposes of Clause 4.2.
findings.why_risky: Disallowing email notice makes it easy to accidentally miss the formal non-renewal deadline, especially given cross-border physical mail requirements between Malaysia and Singapore.
findings.standard: Notice should be permitted by ordinary written methods, including verified email.
findings.suggested_ask: Please allow notice of non-renewal to be served by email to a designated contact address.

missing_clauses.title: Vendor IP infringement indemnity
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: If a third party claims that the Provider's tracking devices, portal software, or technology infringe third-party intellectual property rights, you have no contractual protection or defence coverage from the vendor.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a standard vendor indemnity protecting the customer against third-party intellectual property infringement claims arising from the devices or portal.

msa-02-autorenew.disclaimer: This is an automated review to help you prepare. It is not legal advice.

parties: RIMBUN PAGI CAFE GROUP SDN. BHD.

verdict.headline: High-risk contract: customer pays for custom app development but owns no IP, faces uncapped liability, and bears extreme one-sided terms.
summary: The vendor retains ownership of custom software paid for by the customer, delivers no source code, and can take down the app upon termination.

Liability is entirely one-sided: the vendor caps liability at just one month of fees while customer liability is uncapped, and the customer must indemnify the vendor even for the vendor's own negligence.
The vendor provides zero indemnity against third-party IP infringement claims, exposing the customer to significant legal risk.

findings.title: Vendor retains ownership of custom deliverables and source code
findings.quote: All Intellectual Property Rights in the Deliverables, including any software developed specifically for the Customer, shall vest in and remain with the Vendor.
findings.why_risky: You are paying for custom app development, but you will not own the software. Your licence ends when the contract ends, the vendor keeps the source code, and the vendor can take your app off the app stores.
findings.standard: Custom deliverables developed specifically for the customer should transfer to the customer upon payment, along with source code, subject only to a background IP licence for vendor pre-existing tools.
findings.suggested_ask: Please confirm that all deliverables created specifically for us belong to us on payment, with a continuing licence to any vendor tools built into them, and that our data remains ours.

findings.title: One-sided liability limitations protecting only the vendor
findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement limits the Customer's liability to the Vendor, and the limitations in Clauses 7.1 and 7.2 apply to the Vendor only.
findings.why_risky: Your liability to the vendor is completely uncapped and includes indirect losses, while the vendor's liability is severely restricted.
findings.standard: Limitations of liability and indirect loss exclusions must apply equally to both parties.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the liability cap and indirect loss exclusions mutual so that the same limits protect both parties.

findings.title: Customer indemnifies vendor even for vendor's own negligence
findings.quote: The Customer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Vendor, its affiliates and their officers and employees from and against any and all losses, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses (including legal fees) arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, the Application or the Customer's business, whether or not caused by the negligence of the Vendor.
findings.why_risky: You are forced to pay for all vendor losses, including situations directly caused by the vendor's own careless mistakes or negligence.
findings.standard: Customer indemnities should strictly cover third-party claims arising from customer-provided data or materials, and must explicitly exclude losses caused by the vendor's negligence or breach.
findings.suggested_ask: Please limit the customer's indemnity to third-party claims caused by our own data or breach, and exclude losses caused by the vendor's negligence.

findings.title: Vendor excludes IP infringement indemnity entirely
findings.quote: The Vendor gives no indemnity to the Customer in respect of any matter, including any claim that the Application infringes the intellectual property rights of a third party.
findings.why_risky: If the vendor infringes a third party's software patent, copyright, or trade mark in the application, you bear the entire legal and financial fallout without vendor protection.
findings.standard: Vendors should standardly provide an indemnity protecting the customer if the software or deliverables infringe third-party IP rights.
findings.suggested_ask: Please add the vendor's standard IP infringement indemnity to protect us if the application infringes any third-party intellectual property.

findings.title: Short 60-day warranty period
findings.quote: The Vendor warrants that the Application will materially conform to the SOW for sixty (60) days after acceptance of the final phase, and will correct any material non-conformity reported in that period.
findings.why_risky: Sixty days is shorter than the standard 90-day defect correction window for custom software development.
findings.standard: A balanced warranty period is typically at least 90 days after delivery or acceptance.
findings.suggested_ask: Please extend the warranty defect fix period from 60 days to 90 days post-acceptance.

missing_clauses.title: Comprehensive personal data handling and deletion terms
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The agreement collects End User Data from cafe customers but lacks specific timelines for data breach notifications (e.g. within 48 hours) and contains no clear terms requiring return or secure deletion of customer personal data upon termination under the PDPA.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a data protection clause: processing only on our instructions, reasonable security, breach notice within 48 hours, approved subcontractors, and return or deletion of data at the end.

missing_clauses.title: Exit and data transition assistance
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The contract does not provide a transition grace period or obligations for the vendor to export and return end-user records and customer data upon termination.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a 30-day window and vendor assistance to export all customer and end-user data in a standard usable format upon termination.

parties: ORKID SENYUM DENTAL GROUP SDN. BHD.

verdict.headline: One-sided termination rights and an aggressive liability cap favor the vendor.
summary: The vendor can walk away with just 7 days of notice, while you must give 90 days to terminate for convenience.
The vendor caps its liability at only 3 months of fees, which also limits compensation if staff damage clinic equipment.
Payment terms are aggressive, requiring settlement in 14 days with steep 2% monthly interest plus collection fees.

findings.title: Unbalanced termination for convenience notice periods
findings.quote: The Contractor may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving the Client seven (7) days' written notice.
findings.why_risky: The vendor can leave your five dental clinics without cleaning services on only 7 days' notice, while you are forced to give 90 days' notice under Clause 10.2 to exit.
findings.standard: Both parties should have equal notice periods for termination for convenience, typically between 30 and 90 days.
findings.suggested_ask: Please give both parties the same notice period of 30 or 60 days to terminate for convenience.

findings.title: Low vendor liability cap including clinic property damage
findings.quote: Subject to Clause 7.1, the Contractor's total liability for all claims under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to three (3) months of the Monthly Fee, and the Contractor shall not be liable for any indirect loss, loss of profit or loss of business.
findings.why_risky: A cap of 3 months' fees is very low for physical premises operations where expensive dental equipment could be damaged by vendor staff, despite public liability insurance.
findings.standard: Balanced contracts set liability caps at 12 months of fees or align property damage liability with the vendor's required insurance policy limits.
findings.suggested_ask: Please increase the liability cap to 12 months' fees, and exclude physical property damage covered by your RM 1,000,000 public liability insurance from this cap.

findings.title: Short payment window and high late interest with collection costs
findings.quote: Late payments shall bear interest at the rate of two per cent (2%) per month from the due date until the date of payment, and the Client shall also reimburse the Contractor's collection costs.
findings.why_risky: Combined with a short 14-day payment window, an interest rate of 2% per month (about 24% per year) plus unspecified collection costs is punitive.
findings.standard: Payment terms are typically 30 days from invoice, with late interest capped at 0.5% to 1% per month after a written reminder.
findings.suggested_ask: Please set payment at 30 days from invoice, reduce late interest to no more than 1% a month, and remove the automatic reimbursement of collection costs.

findings.title: No right to withhold disputed invoice amounts
findings.quote: The Client shall pay each invoice in full within fourteen (14) days of the invoice date, without any deduction or set-off.
findings.why_risky: You are forced to pay billing errors or disputed amounts immediately, losing leverage if service was not delivered or was substandard.
findings.standard: The customer should have the right to withhold disputed amounts in good faith while paying undisputed fees.
findings.suggested_ask: Please allow us to withhold disputed invoice amounts in good faith while paying the undisputed balance.

missing_clauses.title: Data breach notification mechanism
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Vendor staff operate inside dental clinics where sensitive patient data exists. The contract lacks a requirement for the vendor to notify you within a defined timeframe (such as 48 to 72 hours) if staff access or expose personal data.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a commitment to notify us in writing within 48 hours if your staff discover or cause any personal data breach.

msa-04-scanned.disclaimer: This is an automated review to help you prepare. It is not legal advice.
